# Foreign Policy

> > Foreign Policy is a leading magazine and digital platform covering global affairs, international relations, geopolitics, and world events.

Foreign Policy provides in-depth analysis, commentary, and breaking news on international security, Middle East politics, diplomacy, terrorism, energy policy, and global economic trends. The publication features expert perspectives on U.S. foreign relations, regional conflicts, and emerging threats to international stability.

## Key Topics

- Middle East Politics
- Iran Nuclear Program
- Iraq War
- U.S.-Iran Relations
- International Security
- Terrorism and Al-Qaeda
- Bush Administration Foreign Policy
- Diplomatic Crisis Management
- Energy Investment and Oil Production
- Syria Conflict
- Afghanistan
- Arab Spring Transitions
- U.S.-China Relations
- Middle East Democracy and Reform

## Middle East Politics & Security

- [Will al Qaeda's Disowned Syria Affiliate Rival Its Old Boss?](https://foreignpolicy.com/2014/02/03/will-al-qaedas-disowned-syria-affiliate-rival-its-old-boss): Analysis of ISIS split from al Qaeda and Zawahiri's leadership challenges
- [The post-Iraq mindset: temporary containment](https://foreignpolicy.com/2006/04/18/the-post-iraq-mindset-temporary-containment): Luttwak on Iran containment strategy and post-Iraq military restraint
- [Trading Places](https://foreignpolicy.com/2014/02/04/trading-places): Tunisia-Egypt comparison on Arab Spring transitions and trade vs. aid
- [Will Israeli voters stay home?](https://foreignpolicy.com/2006/03/27/will-israeli-voters-stay-home): Analysis of voter turnout concerns in Israeli elections amid Kadima rise
- [Brutal dictator, welcome to Washington.](https://foreignpolicy.com/2006/04/15/brutal-dictator-welcome-to-washington): Rice meets Equatorial Guinea dictator Obiang amid human rights concerns
- [Freedom on the run?](https://foreignpolicy.com/2006/04/12/freedom-on-the-run): Doha Forum analysis on Middle East democracy and Arab reform challenges

## Daily Morning Briefs

- [Morning brief, Tuesday April 25](https://foreignpolicy.com/2006/04/25/morning-brief-tuesday-april-25): Daily news brief on Iran nuclear program, Ahmadinejad, and Mideast security
- [Morning brief, Monday, May8](https://foreignpolicy.com/2006/05/08/morning-brief-monday-may8): Daily brief on Hayden CIA nomination, Iraq violence, and ethanol policy
- [Morning Brief, Thursday, May 25](https://foreignpolicy.com/2006/05/25/morning-brief-thursday-may-25): Iran nuclear diplomacy with Larijani and US-Iran relations under Abbas
- [Morning brief, Thursday April 20th](https://foreignpolicy.com/2006/04/20/morning-brief-thursday-april-20th): Hu Jintao US visit, China-Taiwan tensions, and bilateral trade relations

## U.S. Defense & National Security

- [New Nuclear Scandal Rocks Navy](https://foreignpolicy.com/2014/02/05/new-nuclear-scandal-rocks-navy): U.S. Navy nuclear personnel cheating scandal in Charleston, South Carolina
- [Friday Flickr: Kabul](https://foreignpolicy.com/2006/05/27/friday-flickr-kabul): Photo essay on Kabul violence and Red Cross humanitarian prosthetics aid

## Energy & Economic Policy

- [Canada's oil sands](https://foreignpolicy.com/2006/04/06/canadas-oil-sands): Canada's oil sands production and energy investment opportunities
- [More on oil](https://foreignpolicy.com/2006/05/02/more-on-oil): Oil supply-demand dynamics, peak oil debate, and energy investment trends
- [Tom DeLay's energy analysis](https://foreignpolicy.com/2006/05/08/tom-delays-energy-analysis): Tom DeLay on offshore drilling politics in Alaska, Florida, California

## Commentary & Analysis

- [Quotable …](https://foreignpolicy.com/2006/05/25/quotable-5): Notable quote on Enron scandal and Jeffrey Skilling corporate fraud case
- [Quotable](https://foreignpolicy.com/2006/05/09/quotable-6): Ahmadinejad letter to Bush analyzed in diplomatic correspondence context

## Optional
